units: Deut. R. s. 2, end אבל ביוה״כ … הן אומרים אותו בפ׳ וכ׳ but on the Day of Atonement … they say it openly (in a loud voice), Blessed be the name of his glorious kingdom, (opp. בלחישה (v. חֲשַׁאי).—Esp. בפ׳ publicly, opp. בצינעה.
<cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 2:36">Ib.</cite> <he>אל תתקשטי בה בפ׳ וכ׳</he> do not adorn thyself with it in public, but only in the house.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 74a:14">Snh. 74ᵃ</cite> <he>אבל בפ׳ אפי׳ מצוה וכ׳</he> but if a Jew is forced to transgress a religious law in public, he must surrender his life even for a minor law; <cite ref="Sanhedrin 74b:2">ib.ᵇ</cite> <he>וכמה פ׳</he> and the presence of how many is required to call it a public act? <cite ref="Sanhedrin 74b:4">Ib.</cite> <he>אין פ׳ פחותה וכ׳</he> a public is no less than ten persons.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 74b:4">Ib.</cite> <he>והא אסתר פ׳ הואי</he> but was not Esther’s act (when she was forced to marry king Ahasverus) a public one? <cite ref="Chagigah 5a:12">Ḥag. 5ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Ecclesiastes 12:14">Koh. XII, 14</cite>) <he>זה הנותן צדקה לעני בפ׳</he> this refers to one who gives charity to a poor man in public (the Lord judges whether this be a good or a bad deed).
